items.title: Section: The Aspiration to Act and the Aspiration of Correct Comprehensive Practice — Closing Four of Five, Opening the Tenfold Great Vow

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願能無倒思擇諸法，願於境界修無量等殊勝善法，是名所行願。若諸菩薩，願於當來攝受一切菩薩善法，攝受一切所有功德。若總若別所有正願，是名正願。菩薩大願，當知即從正願所出。此復十種。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who aspire to investigate every phenomenon without distortion, and to cultivate boundless, excellent, wholesome practices amid every circumstance — this is called the aspiration to act. Bodhisattvas who aspire, in the future, to gather in every wholesome quality belonging to the bodhisattva path, and to gather in every excellent merit whatsoever, whether in their totality or individually — this is called correct aspiration. One should understand that a bodhisattva's great vow issues directly from this correct aspiration. This is, further, of ten kinds.

items.title: Section: The Ten Great Vows Open — Venerating Every Buddha, Safeguarding the Teaching Itself From Ever Breaking, and Vowing to Descend Through the Eight Classical Phases

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願於當來以一切種上妙供具，供養無量無邊如來，當知是名第一大願。若諸菩薩，願於當來攝受防護諸佛世尊所有正法，傳持法眼令無斷壞，當知是名第二正願。若諸菩薩，願於當來從覩史多天宮降下，如前乃至入大涅槃，當知是名第三大願。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will venerate countless, boundless buddhas with every kind of supreme, wondrous offering — one should understand this to be called the first great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will gather in and safeguard the true teaching belonging to every buddha and world-honoured one, transmitting the very eye of the dharma so that it never breaks or is destroyed — one should understand this to be called the second great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will descend from the palace of Tuṣita heaven and, exactly as already described, proceed all the way through to entering complete nirvāṇa — one should understand this to be called the third great vow.

items.title: Section: Vowing Every Bodhisattva Practice Without Exception, and Maturing Every Being According to Their Own Spiritual Lineage

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願於當來行一切種菩薩正行，當知是名第四大願。若諸菩薩，願於當來普能成熟一切有情，當知是名第五大願。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will practise every kind of correct bodhisattva conduct — one should understand this to be called the fourth great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will universally mature all sentient beings — one should understand this to be called the fifth great vow.

items.title: Section: Manifesting Everywhere in Whatever Guise Actually Helps, and Purifying Every Buddha-Land Across a Buddha's Own Three Bodies

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願於當來一切世界皆能示現，當知是名第六大願。若諸菩薩，願於當來普能淨修一切佛土，當知是名第七大願。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will be able to manifest across every world — one should understand this to be called the sixth great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will universally purify and cultivate every buddha-land — one should understand this to be called the seventh great vow.

items.title: Section: The Final Three Vows Close the Great Vow and the Entire Thirteenth Topic — Unity Among Every Bodhisattva, Effort Never Wasted, and Swift Awakening

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願於當來一切菩薩，皆同一種意樂加行趣入大乘，當知是名第八大願。若諸菩薩，願於當來所有一切無倒加行皆不唐捐，當知是名第九大願。若諸菩薩，願於當來速證無上正等菩提，當知是名第十大願。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, all bodhisattvas will share the identical aspiration and practice, entering the great vehicle together as one — one should understand this to be called the eighth great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, every undistorted effort they undertake will never be wasted — one should understand this to be called the ninth great vow. Bodhisattvas who vow that, in the future, they will swiftly attain supreme, correct awakening — one should understand this to be called the tenth great vow.

items.title: Section: The Three Concentrations Open — Emptiness, Resting the Mind Where Every Verbally-Labelled Essence Genuinely Falls Away

items.zh: 云何菩薩空三摩地？謂諸菩薩觀一切事，遠離一切言說自性，唯有諸法離言自性，心正安住。是名菩薩空三摩地。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's concentration of emptiness? Bodhisattvas who, observing every matter, see it free of every verbally-labelled essence, and who settle the mind correctly, resting solely in the wordless essence belonging to every phenomenon — this is called a bodhisattva's concentration of emptiness.

items.title: Section: Wishlessness — Refusing to Wish for Any Future Rebirth Within Conditioned Existence's Own Contaminated, Wearying Round

items.zh: 云何菩薩無願三摩地？謂諸菩薩，即等隨觀離言自性所有諸事，由邪分別所起煩惱，及以眾苦所攝受故，皆為無量過失所污；於當來世不願為先，心正安住。是名菩薩無願三摩地。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's concentration of wishlessness? Bodhisattvas who, observing every matter resting in its own wordless essence, recognise that these very matters, arising from mistaken discrimination's own afflictions and encompassed by manifold suffering, are thoroughly tainted by countless faults — and who, on this basis, settle the mind correctly by placing the refusal to wish for any of this in future lives foremost — this is called a bodhisattva's concentration of wishlessness.

items.title: Section: Signlessness — Resting Where Every Discriminated Characteristic Has Permanently Fallen Silent

items.zh: 云何菩薩無相三摩地？謂諸菩薩，即正思惟離言自性所有諸事，一切分別戲論眾相永滅寂靜，如實了知，心正安住。是名菩薩無相三摩地。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's concentration of signlessness? Bodhisattvas who correctly reflect on every matter resting in its own wordless essence, correctly and thoroughly know that every characteristic produced by conceptual discrimination and its elaboration has permanently and peacefully ceased, and settle the mind correctly on this very point — this is called a bodhisattva's concentration of signlessness.

items.title: Section: Why Exactly Three, No More and No Fewer — Mapping Each Concentration to What Genuinely Exists and What Never Did

items.zh: 問：何故唯立三三摩地，無過無增？答：法有二種。謂有、非有。有為、無為名之為有，我及我所名為非有。於有為中，有無願故，可厭逆故，當知依此建立無願三摩地。於無為中，願涅槃故，正樂攝故，當知依此建立無相三摩地。於非有事，菩薩不願，亦無無願。然於非有，菩薩如實見為非有。依此見故，當知建立空三摩地。
items.en: Question: Why are exactly three concentrations established, neither more nor fewer? Answer: Phenomena are of two kinds, existent and nonexistent. Conditioned and unconditioned reality together are called existent; a self and what belongs to that self are called nonexistent. Regarding conditioned existence, since there is genuine wishlessness towards it, and since it is genuinely wearying, one should understand that the concentration of wishlessness is established with respect to it. Regarding unconditioned reality, since nirvāṇa is genuinely wished for, and since it is embraced with genuine delight, one should understand that the concentration of signlessness is established with respect to it. Regarding what is nonexistent, bodhisattvas neither wish for it nor refuse to wish for it; rather, bodhisattvas correctly see it as simply nonexistent. On the basis of this seeing, one should understand that the concentration of emptiness is established.

items.title: Section: A Bodhisattva Must Also Understand the Lesser Vehicles' Own Version of These Same Three Concentrations — Closing Topic Fourteen and Fascicle 45 in Full

items.zh: 如是菩薩於此三種三摩地中精勤修學，於是建立如實了知。於餘行相三三摩地如實悟入，安立理趣如實悟入，修習理趣如實了知。謂於其中，諸聲聞眾精勤修學及圓滿證。
items.en: In this way, bodhisattvas, diligently cultivating these three concentrations, correctly and thoroughly know them as thus established. Regarding the three concentrations in their other, differing mode, bodhisattvas correctly and thoroughly enter into their doctrinal framework, and correctly and thoroughly know their actual method of cultivation — that is to say, regarding this same mode, śrāvaka practitioners diligently train in it and thereby reach complete realisation.

blocks.text: The ten great vows, close relatives of the vows in the *Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, and then the three concentrations: emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness. Fascicle 45 ends today.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "I vow to learn the countless dharma gates" is the bodhisattva's aspiration to act.

"Vowing to gather in and safeguard the true dharma of all buddhas, transmitting the dharma-eye so it never breaks": the second vow. The descent through the phases of a buddha's life (Day 401) is vowed here.
Every bodhisattva practice, without exception; every being matured according to their own lineage.
Manifesting in whatever form helps, and purifying every buddha-land.

Unity with all bodhisattvas, effort never wasted, and swift awakening. Venerable Miào Jìng: "never wasted" means no effort is in vain; all bears fruit. But if the mind grasps, the merit cannot reach its full extent.
"Observing every matter as free of every verbally-labelled essence, the mind rests correctly in the wordless essence alone."
Master Cháng Bǎi: the root of saṃsāra is mistaken discrimination; when it ceases, all the suffering of saṃsāra ceases.
The mind rests where every discriminated characteristic has fallen silent.

Wishlessness is set up towards conditioned existence, which is wearying; signlessness towards the unconditioned, since nirvāṇa is peace. Venerable Miào Jìng: here emptiness refers to the absence of self and of what belongs to self.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the śrāvaka version does not stress the wordless nature of phenomena; it directly observes that self and its belongings are absent. The bodhisattva must understand this version too.

Reliance, skilful means, retention, vows, concentration. The thread running through all of it is today's first concentration: the verbal label is empty, the wordless reality is not. Fascicle 46 continues the factors of awakening.

quiz.q: Master Cháng Bǎi matches the "aspiration to act" with which of the four great vows?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "I vow to learn the countless dharma gates" is the bodhisattva's aspiration to act. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first clause concerns understanding, the second practice.

quiz.q: What is the second of the ten great vows?
options: safeguarding every buddha's teaching, transmitting the dharma-eye unbroken
quiz.why: "Vowing to gather in and safeguard the true dharma of all buddhas, transmitting the dharma-eye so it never breaks" — the second great vow. Venerable Miào Jìng: the true dharma is great wisdom, hence an "eye" — it knows which road is dangerous and which safe.

quiz.q: On the ninth vow — "every undistorted effort never wasted" — what does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: never in vain — but if the mind grasps, the merit cannot yield supreme awakening
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "never wasted" means no effort is in vain — all bears fruit; but if the mind grasps, the merit cannot reach supreme awakening. Master Cháng Bǎi: the three spheres empty in every perfection.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define the bodhisattva's concentration of emptiness?
options: seeing every matter free of verbal essence, resting in the wordless essence alone
quiz.why: "Observing every matter as free of every verbally-labelled essence, the mind rests correctly in the wordless essence alone." Venerable Miào Jìng: "matter" means the dependent nature — all causally arisen phenomena.

quiz.q: Why exactly three concentrations? On what are wishlessness and signlessness based?
options: conditioned is wearying — wishlessness; nirvāṇa is wished for — signlessness; self and its belongings seen as nonexistent — emptiness
quiz.why: Wishlessness is established towards conditioned existence, which is wearying; signlessness towards the unconditioned, since nirvāṇa is wished for; emptiness on seeing the nonexistent (self and its belongings) as nonexistent. Venerable Miào Jìng: we turn away from the conditioned and delight in the unconditioned.

quiz.q: §62 bases emptiness on "self and its belongings are nonexistent," unlike §59's "verbal essence." How do the lectures view this?
options: Miào Jìng: here emptiness refers to non-self and non-belonging; Cháng Bǎi: self and its belongings never exist — "nonexistent"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: here the concentration of emptiness refers to non-self and the absence of what belongs to self. Master Cháng Bǎi: self and its belongings fundamentally do not exist — they are "nonexistent." §59 frames emptiness by the wordless essence; §62 by self and belongings.

quiz.q: §63: bodhisattvas also know the "other mode" practised by śrāvakas. How does Master Cháng Bǎi say it differs?
options: it doesn't stress the wordless nature of phenomena, but directly observes that self and its belongings are unfindable
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not emphasise the wordless nature of phenomena but directly observes that self and its belongings are unfindable, reflecting on the five aggregates as impermanent and suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng: śrāvakas attain them through the four fruits.
